newsitem.title: USA: Superior raises food service coffee prices.
newsitem.headline: Superior raises food service coffee prices.

text.p: Superior Coffee and Foods, a division of Sara Lee Corp, said Monday it raised its food service channel coffee prices due to tightness of supply and surging prices in the futures market.

"In early January, coffee was trading around 115 to 118 cents (per lb), now we are seeing sustained prices in the 130s," a company spokesman said. "We are concerned that we have seen the lows. The big thing is just how tight it is. It is a challenge getting coffee."
The spokesman said Superior raised coffee prices in its food service channel by between 20 and 40 cents a lb depending on the blend based on the cost of raw materials.
Arabica coffee futures prices at Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange have risen some 30 percent since early December as U.S. consumer coffee inventories hovered at low levels.
Normally, coffee futures ease at this time of year, as the flow of new-crop coffee out of Latin America increases and stockpiles build.

But some industry analysts said aggressive purchasing by European roasters had absorbed some of the new-crop supply, helping to keep U.S. consumer supplies depleted. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk, 212-859-1640))
